text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch exports in July and August sharply higher than year earlier. (p1)
- ABN AMRO bank suspends three client advisors and sacks another on suspicion of fraud at its diamond office in Amsterdam. (p1)
- Publisher VNU touted as possible candidate to inject capital into Russian-based Dutch publishing house Independent Media. (p1)
- Interest groups in South-Limburg province urge cabinet to reconsider plans for tough restrictions on night-flights at Beek Airport. (p1)
- Trading house Hagemeyer mothballs loss-giving Borsumij Textiles unit as attempts to sell it fail. (p3)
- Sale price of state-owned information technology firm Roccade probably lower due to losses caused by failed launch of salary administration software. (p3)
- Agricultural trading firm Alanheri reports improved third qtr results and confident on full year earnings. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- FNV union fears loss of 65 jobs at Philips Electronics plant in Oss. (p2)
- Royal Dutch/Shell seriously interested in taking over British Gas -- Sunday Telegraph. (p2)
- Dutch Railways and supermarket chain Hermans Group consider setting up supermarkets near stations. (p2)
- Key maker Ankerslot celebrates 50th anniversary with the introduction of an electronic key. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Main political party leaders concerned about political situation on Aruba. (p1)
- Director of concrete plant Betonson dismissed by board. (p13)
TROUW
- Parliament still undecided on sending troops to Zaire. (p3)
- Bank for international payments (BIS) warns central banks to be aware of which businesses and organisations are involved in virtual-money transactions. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm has 850 million guilder 1997 windfall. (p1)
- Brewer Grolsch to build new brewery in Aruba. (p11)
